title: Trabeculectomy: The Gold Standard Filtration Surgery + Trabeculectomy: The Go...
summary: Trabeculectomy remains the definitive filtration procedure for uncontrolled glaucoma. This masterpiece of microsurgery creates a guarded fistula to redirect aqueous humor from the anterior chamber to the subconjunctival space. A comprehensive guide to the filtering procedure for medically uncontrolled glaucoma. This masterclass covers anatomy, surgical technique, and the critical post-operative management required for success.

sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Trabeculectomy is a guarded filtering procedure. It involves the creation of a partial-thickness scleral flap and a surgical excision of a block of trabecular meshwork (trabeculectomy), along with a peripheral iridectomy, to facilitate aqueous drainage into a subconjunctival filtering bleb.

sections.title: Red Flags (Post-Op)
content: Flat anterior chamber (Seidel positive)
Endophthalmitis (pain, vitritis, hypopyon)
Suprachoroidal hemorrhage (pain, profound hypotony)
Malignant glaucoma (shallow AC with high IOP)
Bleb leak or infection

sections.title: Surgical Technique: Step-by-Step
content: 1. Conjunctival peritomy: Fornix or limbus-based.
2. Scleral flap creation: Partial thickness rectangular or triangular (usually 3x3mm).
3. Antimetabolite application: MMC (0.2–0.4 mg/mL) or 5-FU under the flap.
4. Sclerostomy: Excision of the deep scleral block and trabecular meshwork.
5. Peripheral Iridectomy: To prevent iris plugging of the ostium.
6. Scleral flap suturing: Titratable tension (e.g., 10-0 Nylon).
7. Conjunctival closure: Watertight closure (e.g., 9-0 Vicryl).

content.explanation: W: Wound check, A: Antimetabolite (MMC), T: Tension (suture), E: Excision (trabecular block), R: Re-form (AC)

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Always perform Seidel test with Fluorescein to rule out leaks.
Post-op steroid usage is critical for modulation of wound healing.
Suture lysis (via laser) is a vital tool for titration of flow in the first 2-4 weeks.
Cataract progression is significantly accelerated by trabeculectomy.
Warn patients regarding lifelong risk of bleb-related endophthalmitis.

sections.title: Definition & Indications
sections.content: Trabeculectomy is a full-thickness or guarded filtration procedure designed to create an alternative drainage pathway for aqueous humor, bypassing the diseased trabecular meshwork. Indicated for patients with progressive visual field loss or uncontrolled intraocular pressure (IOP) despite maximum tolerated medical therapy (MTMT) and laser trabeculoplasty.

sections.title: Red Flags: Immediate Post-op
content: Flat anterior chamber (Seidel-positive bleb leak).
Choroidal detachment (kissing choroidals).
Hypotony (IOP < 5 mmHg) leading to maculopathy.
Malignant Glaucoma (Aqueous misdirection).
Endophthalmitis (pain, vitritis, hypopyon).

content.explanation: S: Seidel (Leak), S: Shallow (Chamber), S: Suprachoroidal (Hemorrhage/Effusion), S: Sepsis (Endophthalmitis).
